back_log.description: Listen backlog of mysqld (capped by net.core.somaxconn).
back_log.precondition: accept queue overflows during the run (listen_drops > 0)
back_log.when: bursts of new connections dropped by the accept queue

binlog_cache_size.memory_cost: per active connection with a transaction (binary log on)

binlog_group_commit_sync_delay.description: Microseconds to wait to grow binlog commit groups.
binlog_group_commit_sync_delay.when: binary log on, commit-bound at high concurrency

binlog_group_commit_sync_no_delay_count.description: Stop waiting once this many transactions are queued.

binlog_row_image.description: FULL logs all columns; MINIMAL only changed + PK.
binlog_row_image.safety_note: Row events no longer carry full before/after images; some CDC / audit consumers break.

binlog_transaction_dependency_history_si.description: Rows kept in the WRITESET dependency history for parallel replication.

client:os:datadir_fs.description: Client host: Filesystem of the data directory on the experiment device (scope 'filesystem' only).

client:os:fs.aio-max-nr.description: Client host: System-wide limit of in-flight asynchronous I/O requests (InnoDB native AIO).

client:os:hugepages.description: Client host: Number of 2 MiB huge pages reserved (used by the buffer pool when large_pages=ON).

client:os:kernel.numa_balancing.description: Client host: Automatic NUMA page migration (multi-socket hosts).

client:os:kernel.sched_autogroup_enabled.description: Client host: Group CPU time per terminal session (desktop feature).

client:os:malloc.description: Client host: Memory allocator for mysqld: glibc[:arena_max=N], jemalloc[:MALLOC_CONF], tcmalloc, mimalloc (LD_PRELOAD).

client:os:mount_barrier.description: Client host: ext4 write barriers (OFF = nobarrier: DURABILITY TRADE-OFF).

client:os:mount_noatime.description: Client host: Mount the data directory filesystem with noatime.

client:os:net.core.default_qdisc.description: Client host: Default queueing discipline (fq pairs with bbr).

client:os:net.core.netdev_budget.description: Client host: Packets processed per softirq round.

client:os:net.core.netdev_budget_usecs.description: Client host: Time budget per softirq round.

client:os:net.core.netdev_max_backlog.description: Client host: Per-CPU packet backlog before softnet drops.

client:os:net.core.rmem_max.description: Client host: Max receive buffer an application may set.

client:os:net.core.rps_sock_flow_entries.description: Client host: RFS global flow table.

client:os:net.core.somaxconn.description: Client host: Upper bound of listen backlogs (MySQL back_log is capped by it).

client:os:net.core.wmem_max.description: Client host: Max send buffer an application may set.

client:os:net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range.description: Client host: Ephemeral ports for outgoing connections (clients).

client:os:net.ipv4.tcp_congestion_contro.description: Client host: TCP congestion control algorithm (cubic / bbr).

client:os:net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_intvl.description: Client host: Interval between keepalive probes.

client:os:net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_probes.description: Client host: Keepalive probes before the connection is dropped.

client:os:net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time.description: Client host: Idle time before TCP keepalive probes.

client:os:net.ipv4.tcp_rmem.description: Client host: TCP receive buffer min/default/max (autotuning ceiling).

client:os:net.ipv4.tcp_slow_start_after_.description: Client host: Shrink the congestion window after idle (hurts pooled connections over WAN).

client:os:net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse.description: Client host: Reuse TIME_WAIT sockets for new outgoing connections (clients).

client:os:net.ipv4.tcp_wmem.description: Client host: TCP send buffer min/default/max.

client:os:net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max.description: Client host: Connection tracking table size (firewalled hosts).

client:os:net_irq_cpus.description: Client host: CPUs that handle the network card interrupts (auto / CPU list); irqbalance is stopped while managed.

client:os:read_ahead_kb.description: Client host: OS read-ahead of the data device (no effect on InnoDB data files opened with O_DIRECT).

client:os:rps.description: Client host: Receive Packet Steering over all CPUs for every RX queue (spreads softirq).

client:os:scheduler.description: Client host: Block I/O scheduler of the data device.

client:os:swapfile.description: Client host: Extra swap file managed by the agent (size, 0 = none): room for cold memory so caches can grow.

client:os:thp.description: Client host: Transparent Huge Pages (never / madvise / always).

client:os:vm.dirty_background_bytes.description: Client host: Dirty page cache that starts background writeback (affects buffered binlog/redo writes).

client:os:vm.dirty_background_ratio.description: Client host: Dirty page cache (% of memory) that starts background writeback (used when dirty_background_bytes is 0).

client:os:vm.dirty_bytes.description: Client host: Dirty page cache at which writers are throttled.

client:os:vm.dirty_expire_centisecs.description: Client host: Age at which dirty page cache must be written back.

client:os:vm.dirty_ratio.description: Client host: Dirty page cache (% of memory) at which writers are throttled (used when dirty_bytes is 0).

client:os:vm.dirty_writeback_centisecs.description: Client host: Interval of the background writeback thread.

client:os:vm.min_free_kbytes.description: Client host: Free memory the kernel keeps for atomic (network/driver) allocations.

client:os:vm.swappiness.description: Client host: Kernel preference for swapping anonymous memory (1 = only under real pressure).

client:os:zswap.description: Client host: Compressed in-memory cache for swapped pages (off / on[:compressor]): cheaper swap-ins.

disable_log_bin.description: Start without the binary log (option-file switch).
disable_log_bin.safety_note: No binary log: no replication and no point-in-time recovery.
disable_log_bin.when: binary log on and commit or CPU bound; measured +18%

innodb_adaptive_flushing_lwm.description: Redo fill % where adaptive flushing starts.

innodb_adaptive_hash_index.description: Hash index built over hot B-tree pages; helps point lookups, can contend.
innodb_adaptive_hash_index.when: point lookups on a hot set (helps) vs latch contention or analytics (JOB 88% slower with it ON)

innodb_buffer_pool_instances.description: Number of buffer pool partitions; reduces mutex contention.
innodb_buffer_pool_instances.when: many cores with buffer pool mutex contention

innodb_buffer_pool_size.description: Main InnoDB cache for data and index pages.
innodb_buffer_pool_size.memory_cost: direct: its size, plus ~3% for control blocks / page hash / AHI
innodb_buffer_pool_size.when: the working set misses memory (data page reads); too large causes swapping / OOM

innodb_change_buffering.when: insert / update-heavy with secondary indexes and data larger than memory; off measured -23% to -88% on ingest

innodb_checksum_algorithm.safety_note: Page corruption is no longer detected.

innodb_doublewrite.description: Doublewrite buffer protects against torn pages.
innodb_doublewrite.safety_note: Torn (partially written) pages after a crash can no longer be repaired: possible unrecoverable corruption.

innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit.description: 1 = fsync redo at every commit (durable); 2 = write at commit, fsync ~1/s.
innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit.safety_note: Committed transactions from the last ~1 s are lost on an OS crash or power loss (value 0: also on a mysqld crash).
innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit.when: commit-bound load (redo fsync per transaction); measured +26-34%

innodb_flush_method.description: How data files are opened/flushed; O_DIRECT avoids double caching.
innodb_flush_method.safety_note: Skips fsync() after data file writes; safe only when the filesystem persists metadata on its own (XFS/ext4 with O_DIRECT); a crash on other setups can lose file-size changes.
innodb_flush_method.when: double buffering in the page cache; O_DIRECT_NO_FSYNC is a trade-off

innodb_flush_neighbors.description: Flush neighbouring dirty pages together; useless on SSD.

innodb_flush_sync.description: ON: during sync flushing (checkpoint pressure) ignore innodb_io_capacity_max.

innodb_io_capacity.when: flush-bound with disk headroom; raising it on a saturated disk measured -12% to -35%

innodb_io_capacity_max.description: Upper bound of background flushing IOPS when behind.

innodb_log_buffer_size.description: Buffer for redo log records before they are written to disk.
innodb_log_buffer_size.when: large transactions waiting for log buffer space

innodb_log_file_size.description: Size of each redo log file (older MySQL / MariaDB).

innodb_log_files_in_group.description: Number of redo log files (older MySQL).

innodb_log_writer_threads.when: few CPUs under pressure (+10% on 2 vCPU); lost 2-13% at 12-16 vCPU

innodb_lru_scan_depth.description: How far page cleaners scan LRU for free pages per instance.
innodb_lru_scan_depth.when: free-page waits (single-page flushes in user threads)

innodb_max_dirty_pages_pct_lwm.description: Dirty page percentage where pre-flushing starts.

innodb_max_purge_lag.description: History list length above which DML is delayed so purge can catch up (0 = never).
innodb_max_purge_lag.when: history list growth hurting reads; slows writers

innodb_max_purge_lag_delay.description: Maximum delay in microseconds imposed by innodb_max_purge_lag.

innodb_numa_interleave.description: Interleave buffer pool allocation across NUMA nodes.

innodb_parallel_read_threads.description: Threads for parallel clustered index reads (COUNT(*), CHECK TABLE).

innodb_purge_threads.when: history list growing under write load

innodb_read_ahead_threshold.description: Sequential pages accessed in an extent that trigger linear read-ahead.

innodb_redo_log_capacity.description: Total redo log size (MySQL 8.0.30+). Larger = fewer forced checkpoints.
innodb_redo_log_capacity.when: write-heavy load with checkpoint age near capacity (forced flushing); measured +2-10%

innodb_spin_wait_delay.when: latch spinning in the CPU profile

innodb_stats_persistent_sample_pages.description: Pages sampled for persistent index statistics.

innodb_sync_spin_loops.description: Spin iterations before a thread sleeps on a mutex/rw-lock.
innodb_sync_spin_loops.when: latch spinning in the CPU profile

innodb_thread_concurrency.description: Max threads inside InnoDB at once (0 = unlimited).
innodb_thread_concurrency.when: extreme oversubscription; lost in every measured case so far

innodb_use_fdatasync.description: Use fdatasync() instead of fsync() where safe.

join_buffer_size.description: Per-join buffer for joins without usable indexes.
join_buffer_size.memory_cost: per active connection, per join - possibly more than once per query
join_buffer_size.when: joins without usable indexes / hash joins spilling (analytics)

large_pages.description: Allocate the buffer pool from huge pages (needs vm.nr_hugepages and memlock).
large_pages.when: memory-bound work with a large buffer pool (TLB misses); needs measured headroom

max_connections.memory_cost: ~768 KiB base per allowed connection (+ performance_schema ~128 KiB); 2 x CPUs of them assumed active with all per-query buffers
max_connections.when: a benchmark prerequisite; too high wastes memory

max_heap_table_size.description: Max size of MEMORY tables; caps in-memory temp tables too.
max_heap_table_size.memory_cost: per active connection (with tmp_table_size, the lower applies)
max_heap_table_size.precondition: on-disk temporary tables during the run (Created_tmp_disk_tables > 0)

optimizer_switch.description: Optimizer flags (on / off each); the tuner changes them one flag at a time.
optimizer_switch.when: a list of independent optimizer flags: see the optimizer_switch:<flag> entries

optimizer_switch:batched_key_access.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:batched_key_access.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower. With mrr_cost_based=off it is used even when not cheaper
optimizer_switch:batched_key_access.when: joins doing many random index lookups into data larger than memory (needs mrr=on and a join buffer)

optimizer_switch:block_nested_loop.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:block_nested_loop.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.
optimizer_switch:block_nested_loop.when: joins without usable indexes (8.0.20+: controls hash join use)

optimizer_switch:condition_fanout_filter.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:condition_fanout_filter.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower. Estimates change join orders
optimizer_switch:condition_fanout_filter.when: join order estimates on filtered columns (JOB-like multi-joins)

optimizer_switch:derived_condition_pushd.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:derived_condition_pushd.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.

optimizer_switch:derived_merge.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:derived_merge.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.
optimizer_switch:derived_merge.when: derived tables / views merged into the outer query

optimizer_switch:duplicateweedout.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:duplicateweedout.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.

optimizer_switch:engine_condition_pushdo.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:engine_condition_pushdo.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.

optimizer_switch:favor_range_scan.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:favor_range_scan.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.
optimizer_switch:favor_range_scan.when: range scans vs ref access choice (9.x)

optimizer_switch:firstmatch.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:firstmatch.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.

optimizer_switch:hash_join.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:hash_join.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.
optimizer_switch:hash_join.when: equi-joins without usable indexes (no-op on 8.0.20+, see block_nested_loop)

optimizer_switch:hash_set_operations.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:hash_set_operations.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.
optimizer_switch:hash_set_operations.when: UNION / INTERSECT / EXCEPT with large inputs

optimizer_switch:hypergraph_optimizer.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:hypergraph_optimizer.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower. Experimental: plans and supported features differ; debug builds only in many versions
optimizer_switch:hypergraph_optimizer.when: complex multi-way joins (experimental optimizer in 8.0-9.x builds that include it)

optimizer_switch:index_condition_pushdow.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:index_condition_pushdow.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.
optimizer_switch:index_condition_pushdow.when: range scans with extra conditions on index columns (fewer row reads)

optimizer_switch:index_merge.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:index_merge.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.
optimizer_switch:index_merge.when: OR / AND conditions over several indexed columns

optimizer_switch:index_merge_intersectio.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:index_merge_intersectio.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower. Turning it off is a common fix for intersect plans
optimizer_switch:index_merge_intersectio.when: AND over several indexes; known to pick slow intersections on correlated columns

optimizer_switch:index_merge_sort_union.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:index_merge_sort_union.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.
optimizer_switch:index_merge_sort_union.when: OR over ranges on several indexes

optimizer_switch:index_merge_union.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:index_merge_union.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.

optimizer_switch:loosescan.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:loosescan.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.

optimizer_switch:materialization.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:materialization.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.

optimizer_switch:mrr.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:mrr.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.
optimizer_switch:mrr.when: range / ref reads of secondary indexes on disk-bound data (reads in primary-key order)

optimizer_switch:mrr_cost_based.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:mrr_cost_based.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower. Off forces MRR even where it is slower
optimizer_switch:mrr_cost_based.when: forcing MRR / BKA on regardless of cost

optimizer_switch:prefer_ordering_index.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:prefer_ordering_index.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower. Off is a common fix for slow ORDER BY LIMIT plans
optimizer_switch:prefer_ordering_index.when: ORDER BY ... LIMIT choosing an ordering index over a better filter

optimizer_switch:semijoin.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:semijoin.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.

optimizer_switch:skip_scan.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:skip_scan.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.
optimizer_switch:skip_scan.when: range on the second column of a composite index

optimizer_switch:subquery_materializatio.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:subquery_materializatio.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.
optimizer_switch:subquery_materializatio.when: choice between materialization and EXISTS rewrite

optimizer_switch:subquery_to_derived.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:subquery_to_derived.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower. Can slow queries the default plan handled well
optimizer_switch:subquery_to_derived.when: analytics with correlated scalar subqueries in SELECT / WHERE (TPC-H +70%)

optimizer_switch:use_index_extensions.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:use_index_extensions.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower.
optimizer_switch:use_index_extensions.when: secondary indexes used with their implicit primary-key columns

optimizer_switch:use_invisible_indexes.precondition: statements whose plans use this strategy
optimizer_switch:use_invisible_indexes.safety_note: Does not change query results; plans change, so some queries may get slower. On makes the optimizer use indexes marked invisible

os:cpu_affinity.description: CPUs the database process may run on (all / CPU list such as 1-3), e.g. to keep it off the CPUs handling network interrupts.

os:cpu_governor.when: CPU-bound on hosts that scale the clock down

os:datadir_fs.description: Filesystem of the data directory on the experiment device (scope 'filesystem' only).
os:datadir_fs.safety_note: The filesystem may acknowledge writes before they are durable (crash can lose or corrupt recent data).
os:datadir_fs.when: I/O or commit-bound: file system choice changes allocation and journaling

os:fs.aio-max-nr.description: System-wide limit of in-flight asynchronous I/O requests (InnoDB native AIO).

os:hugepages.description: Number of 2 MiB huge pages reserved (used by the buffer pool when large_pages=ON).
os:hugepages.memory_cost: pins 2 MiB per page: unusable by anything else, even when the buffer pool does not use it

os:kernel.sched_autogroup_enabled.description: Group CPU time per terminal session (desktop feature).
os:kernel.sched_autogroup_enabled.when: run-queue waits with other process groups on the host

os:malloc.description: Memory allocator for mysqld: glibc[:arena_max=N], jemalloc[:MALLOC_CONF], tcmalloc, mimalloc (LD_PRELOAD).
os:malloc.when: allocator time in the CPU profile, many threads

os:mount_barrier.description: ext4 write barriers (OFF = nobarrier: DURABILITY TRADE-OFF).
os:mount_barrier.safety_note: Without write barriers a power loss can lose or reorder writes the database already considered durable.
os:mount_barrier.when: commit-bound on disks with a volatile write cache; durability trade-off

os:mount_noatime.description: Mount the data directory filesystem with noatime.

os:net.core.default_qdisc.description: Default queueing discipline (fq pairs with bbr).

os:net.core.netdev_max_backlog.description: Per-CPU packet backlog before softnet drops.

os:net.core.rmem_max.description: Max receive buffer an application may set.

os:net.core.somaxconn.description: Upper bound of listen backlogs (MySQL back_log is capped by it).
os:net.core.somaxconn.precondition: accept queue overflows during the run (listen_drops > 0)

os:net.core.wmem_max.description: Max send buffer an application may set.

os:net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_probes.description: Keepalive probes before the connection is dropped.

os:net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time.description: Idle time before TCP keepalive probes.

os:net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog.precondition: SYN queue drops during the run (syn_drops > 0)

os:net.ipv4.tcp_slow_start_after_idle.description: Shrink the congestion window after idle (hurts pooled connections over WAN).

os:net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse.description: Reuse TIME_WAIT sockets for new outgoing connections (clients).

os:net_irq_cpus.description: CPUs that handle the network card interrupts (auto / CPU list); irqbalance is stopped while managed.

os:read_ahead_kb.description: OS read-ahead of the data device (no effect on InnoDB data files opened with O_DIRECT).

os:rps.description: Receive Packet Steering over all CPUs for every RX queue (spreads softirq).

os:scheduler.description: Block I/O scheduler of the data device.

os:swapfile.description: Extra swap file managed by the agent (size, 0 = none): room for cold memory so caches can grow.
os:swapfile.memory_cost: disk, not memory: lets cold memory be swapped instead of OOM
os:swapfile.when: safety net for memory experiments; no effect without memory pressure

os:transparent_hugepage.when: page-fault / compaction stalls in the kernel profile

os:vm.dirty_background_bytes.description: Dirty page cache that starts background writeback (affects buffered binlog/redo writes).

os:vm.dirty_background_ratio.description: Dirty page cache (% of memory) that starts background writeback (used when dirty_background_bytes is 0).

os:vm.dirty_bytes.description: Dirty page cache at which writers are throttled.
os:vm.dirty_bytes.when: fsync stalls from large page-cache writeback

os:vm.dirty_expire_centisecs.description: Age at which dirty page cache must be written back.

os:vm.dirty_ratio.description: Dirty page cache (% of memory) at which writers are throttled (used when dirty_bytes is 0).

os:vm.dirty_writeback_centisecs.description: Interval of the background writeback thread.

os:vm.min_free_kbytes.description: Free memory the kernel keeps for atomic (network/driver) allocations.

os:vm.swappiness.description: Kernel preference for swapping anonymous memory (1 = only under real pressure).
os:vm.swappiness.when: memory pressure with mysqld memory swapped out

os:zswap.description: Compressed in-memory cache for swapped pages (off / on[:compressor]): cheaper swap-ins.

performance_schema.description: Performance Schema instrumentation (needed for latency measurement).
performance_schema.memory_cost: ~192 MiB fixed + ~128 KiB per allowed connection
performance_schema.safety_note: No statement latency / wait instrumentation: diagnostics and query analysis are lost.
performance_schema.when: CPU-bound, many short statements; measured 3-5% (up to 25% of CPU on 2 vCPU)

ps:profile.description: performance_schema instrumentation: full (server default) or lite (only what the tuner reads: digests, latency histogram, wait summaries); lite loses statement history and memory accounting.
ps:profile.safety_note: performance_schema statement/transaction history and memory accounting are no longer collected (digests, latency histogram and wait summaries stay).
ps:profile.when: as performance_schema, keeping digests and wait summaries

read_rnd_buffer_size.description: Buffer for multi-range reads / sorted row reads.
read_rnd_buffer_size.memory_cost: per active connection, per sorted read

rg:innodb_bg_cpus.description: CPUs for InnoDB background threads via a MySQL resource group (off / CPU list); keeps flushing bursts off the query CPUs.

skip_log_bin.description: Start without the binary log (option-file switch).
skip_log_bin.safety_note: No binary log: no replication and no point-in-time recovery.

skip_name_resolve.description: Skip reverse DNS on connect; host-name grants stop matching.
skip_name_resolve.precondition: measured time in host name resolution
skip_name_resolve.safety_note: Host-name based accounts (user@hostname) stop matching; only IP-based and wildcard grants work.
skip_name_resolve.when: measured time in host name resolution on connect

sort_buffer_size.memory_cost: per active connection, per sort - possibly more than once per query
sort_buffer_size.precondition: sort merge passes during the run (Sort_merge_passes > 0)
sort_buffer_size.when: sort merge passes during the run

sync_binlog.description: fsync binary log every N commit groups (1 = durable).
sync_binlog.safety_note: Binary log events can be lost on an OS crash: replicas and point-in-time recovery diverge from the data.
sync_binlog.when: binary log on and commit-bound (binlog fsync per group)

table_definition_cache.precondition: table definition loading during the run (Opened_table_definitions > 0)
table_definition_cache.when: table definitions loaded during the run

table_open_cache_instances.description: Partitions of the table open cache.

temptable_max_ram.description: RAM the TempTable engine may use before spilling to mmap/disk.
temptable_max_ram.memory_cost: global cap on in-memory temporary tables

thread_cache_size.description: Threads kept for reuse by new connections.

thread_handling.when: connections far above CPU cores with run-queue waits; hurt at low concurrency (-9%)

tmp_table_size.description: Max size of in-memory internal temporary tables.
tmp_table_size.memory_cost: per active connection (one in-memory temporary table), capped by temptable_max_ram
tmp_table_size.precondition: on-disk temporary tables during the run (Created_tmp_disk_tables > 0)
tmp_table_size.when: analytics spilling temporary tables to disk

transaction_isolation.safety_note: Weaker isolation changes what concurrent transactions see; application correctness must be re-validated.
